## Cause

`V3__drop_unused_indexes.sql` (commit 4d99828, "Q3 storage review") dropped `ux_payment_idempotency_key`:

```sql
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_payment_idempotency_key;
```

That index was the enforcement half of the idempotency fix from 5940039. The reasoning in the migration is the trap: the index showed no reads in `pg_stat_user_indexes` because a uniqueness constraint is never *read* as a lookup path — it's checked on write. Dropping it on "zero reads" evidence removed the only guarantee that survives concurrency.

`PaymentService.create` (`src/main/java/mn/payments/PaymentService.java:29`) still does its `existsByIdempotencyKey` check inside the transaction, but that check alone races: under `READ COMMITTED`, two concurrent calls carrying the same key both see `false` and both insert. Commit 5940039's own comment says both halves are needed. Since 4d99828 only one half is there — hence "again."

## Fix

Added `src/main/resources/db/migration/V4__restore_payment_unique_index.sql`, recreating the index. V3 is already applied in production, so it's a new forward migration rather than an edit. `ix_payment_status_created` stays dropped — that one genuinely was an unused lookup index. `mvn -o test` passes.

The migration will fail if duplicate keys were written during the window when the index was missing; that's deliberate — those rows need reconciliation (and refunds) before uniqueness can be re-established. Worth checking before you deploy:

```sql
SELECT idempotency_key, count(*) FROM payment GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1;
```

## One thing I did not touch

`create()` builds the new `Payment` with only `p.setStatus("PENDING")` — it never assigns `id`, `idempotencyKey`, or `amount`, and `Payment` exposes no setters for them. Taken literally, no insert could ever populate `idempotency_key`, which would defeat both the app check and the index. That's been true since the first commit, not a regression, so I assume something outside this tree (a builder or an ORM mapping layer) fills those in. If it doesn't, that's a second, independent cause of double charges and I should fix it — say the word and I will.
